problem.text: Tokenizer construction eagerly builds lookup tables using per-token decoding and repeated backend vocabulary-size queries. The change replaces these operations with batched decoding and cached helpers.

reasoning.text: Reducing Python/backend crossings plausibly explains the claimed faster initialization, but the inspected evidence contains no timing comparison.

impact.text: The optimization also changes cache ownership and the ordinal getter's return behavior; it is not strictly a performance-only substitution.

source_notes.text: The root loading-tokenization entry describes eager vocabulary construction, the whitespace probe, and inherited decode-filter limitations.

PR #13, “Fix a tokenizer issue while converting models without a bos_token_id defined,” reports a separate None-valued BOS failure. Its relationship here is contextual inference based on the shared tokenizer file, not evidence motivating this optimization; the parent already guards that BOS lookup.

limitations: No real Hugging Face tokenizer, initialization benchmark, model generation, or concurrent execution was run. Batched-versus-individual decoding equivalence remains unmeasured.
The scalar check models inspected Python cache and list behavior; it does not execute the repository implementation.
Replacing token-to-string-to-ID round trips with range assumes dense, round-tripping backend IDs. Compatibility with sparse or unusual tokenizer vocabularies is unestablished.

chapters.title: Batching and caching tokenizer lookup construction

claims.text: raw_vocab_size caches the backend size and supplies actual_vocab_size calculation, decode filtering, and table construction. Initialization remains eager: it builds ordinals, special and ordinary piece lists, and the reverse map before returning.

get_fixed_vocab preserves the existing ' t' probe. One token decoding to the probe's two-character length selects singleton sequences; otherwise each ID is decoded after a space-prefix token, whose decoded character length is sliced away. Both paths now issue decode_batch rather than one decode call per ID. The nonempty-probe assertion remains, as does the unguarded indexing of the separately encoded space.

The table getters replace attribute-based early returns with lru_cache. synchronized still surrounds their cache access using the utility's reentrant lock, allowing the special-list getter to call the ordinary getter recursively. get_fixed_vocab and raw_vocab_size themselves have no synchronized decorator.

get_id_to_ord_list now initializes base entries as range(raw_vocab_size), rather than round-tripping through id_to_token and token_to_id. Appended entries retain hexadecimal-byte parsing, single-character ordinals up to 255, and -1 for unsupported pieces or gaps. Thus base entries remain ID-like rather than becoming a general byte decoder.

Whole-parent searches found no ordinal-table consumer beyond construction. Piece-list consumers remain list-compatible: generation_loop indexes sampled IDs; Job indexes completion, healing and stop-token strings; prefix helpers scan or index the list. single_id still consumes the reverse dictionary. However, their shared table construction can duplicate appended entries, as recorded in the finding.

A bounded Python transcription reproduced separate default/explicit-False cache computations mutating one cached vocabulary list: the ordinary table contained two copies of the appended token while the special copy contained one. It also reproduced the ordinal getter returning None despite setting its attribute.

findings.description: The cached decoded vocabulary is mutated by separately cached ordinary-list calls, duplicating appended vocabulary entries during construction.
findings.trigger: A tokenizer has actual_vocab_size greater than raw_vocab_size. Construction calls get_id_to_piece_list(True), which invokes the no-argument form, then calls get_id_to_piece_list(False).
findings.expected_behavior: Each appended ID occupies exactly one table position, and the reverse map points to that ID.
findings.actual_behavior: Both ordinary computations obtain the same get_fixed_vocab list and append the extension again. The special copy predates the second append; the reverse dictionary enumerates the duplicated list and can map an extended piece to its later, incorrect index.

verification.description: Modeled constructor call order, lru_cache argument distinctions, cached-list aliasing and extension.
verification.limits: Synthetic two-token vocabulary with one extension; no tokenizer backend executed.

findings.description: get_id_to_ord_list no longer returns its populated list.
findings.trigger: A caller uses the getter's return value.
findings.expected_behavior: Return the ordinal list, as the parent implementation did.
findings.actual_behavior: The function falls through and its cache stores None. self.id_to_ord is still populated. Whole-parent search found only the constructor call, which discards the return, so no inspected internal consumer fails on this change.

verification.description: Compared removed return statement with the complete parent function and searched callers.

findings.description: The touched decode_ path carries over the earlier entry's ineffective EOS truncation.
findings.trigger: decode receives ordinary tokens both before and after EOS with special rendering disabled.
findings.expected_behavior: The explicit EOS-truncation branch would discard tokens after EOS.
findings.actual_behavior: Filtering removes EOS first, making that branch unreachable; post-EOS tokens remain. Only the vocabulary-size query changes in this commit. Direct callers are the rank-one and rank-two branches of decode; Job also uses decode for incomplete-character recovery, but this does not establish that its stop handling reaches this trigger.

verification.description: Applied the inspected filter to [11,2,12,0,99] with EOS 2, PAD 0 and vocabulary size 50; result was [11,12].
verification.limits: Filtering only; no backend decoding or generation execution.

annotation.summary: Batches vocabulary decoding and caches tokenizer lookup construction, with unmeasured speed benefits, shared-list extension risk, and a removed ordinal-getter return.
